judged_text: Feed items whose link resolves to blank and whose id is also non-HTTP produce url = i.id / nil, and items with a blank or missing title flow into PostCreator under skip_validations: true. With validations skipped, a nil/blank title is not rejected by PostCreator's normal validation, so malformed feed entries can create topics with empty titles (or fail inside the transaction each hour, re-enqueueing the same bad item every poll with no dead-letter or skip counter), poisoning the import stream indefinitely.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Feed items whose link resolves to blank and whose id is also non-HTTP produce url = i.id / nil, and items with a blank or missing title flow into PostCreator under skip_validations: true. With validations skipped, a nil/blank title is not rejected by PostCreator's normal validation, so malformed feed entries can create topics with empty titles (or fail inside the transaction each hour, re-enqueueing the same bad item every poll with no dead-letter or skip counter), poisoning the import stream indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each RSS item is imported via `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post/topic using `PostCreator.new(... title: title, ... skip_validations: true, ...)` with no guard that `title` is present. Because validations are explicitly skipped, a blank/nil `i.title` can result in creating a topic/post with an empty title (or triggering downstream errors) from malformed feed entries. However, the finding’s sub-claim that `url = i.id / nil` will necessarily poison the stream is overstated: if `url` ends up nil or non-HTTP, `TopicEmbed.import` early-returns via `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (nil `=~` just yields nil), so that case is a no-op rather than a guaranteed repeated failure.
